note: Generic form-shooting drills (drills.py); not medical or professional coaching advice.

high.cue: Form the elbow into an L (about 90 deg) at the set point before every rep; check in a mirror.

low.prescription: 3 x 10 lifts from waist to set
low.cue: Load less: the forearm should be roughly vertical at the set point, not folded onto the biceps.

high.prescription: 3 x 12 reps, 1 m from a wall
high.cue: Stand side-on to a wall so the elbow brushes it on the way up: keeps the elbow under the ball.

low.cue: Let the elbow sit slightly in front of the shoulder so the forearm can extend toward the rim.

high.cue: Sit into a quarter squat before the lift; the legs start the shot, the arm finishes it.

low.cue: Dip only to the top of a chair seat: a shallower, quicker load keeps the rhythm one-motion.

high.cue: Hinge slightly at the hips at the set point so the chest stays over the feet.

low.cue: Load with the knees, not the trunk: keep the chest up and the eyes on the rim.

high.cue: Finish with the hips under the shoulders; land where you jumped from.

low.cue: Allow a few degrees of forward lean at release so the shot carries, instead of fading.

high.cue: Release as the arm reaches full extension, not after an extra reach; keep the wrist relaxed.

low.cue: Finish with the elbow above the eyebrow and the wrist above the head before the ball leaves.

high.cue: Start the ball closer to the forehead so the release stays over the head, not pushed out.

low.cue: Extend toward the rim on release; the fingers should finish pointing at the target.

high.cue: No pause at the set point: dip, lift and release in one continuous motion.

low.cue: Say 'one' at the dip and 'two' at release so the load is not rushed.

high.cue: Hold the follow-through until the ball hits the rim, then relax; no rigid over-hold.

low.cue: Hold the finish (hand in the rim) for a full two seconds before dropping the arm.

high.cue: Reach the hand into the cookie jar: a full wrist snap puts backspin on the ball.

low.cue: Snap through the ball without forcing the fingers down; let the follow-through be loose.

high.cue: Shoot on the way up, releasing before the peak of a small hop; save the legs for range.

low.cue: Drive through the balls of the feet so the legs supply the power and the arm stays soft.

high.cue: Extend fully but keep the follow-through loose; a hard lockout stiffens the wrist.

low.cue: Reach the elbow to full extension at release; the arm should look like a straight line to the rim.

low.cue: Finish with the elbow above the eyebrow: the upper arm should point up toward the rim, not straight ahead.

low.cue: Let the legs finish the jump: the ball leaves the hand as you reach the top, not early on the way up.
